title: Stand balusters along a guard so a 51 mm test ball cannot pass through any gap
instruction: Stand the white balusters upright on the oak shoe rail between the two newel posts so that a 51 mm test ball cannot pass through any gap, including the gaps next to the posts, and space them evenly. Use as many of the six balusters as you need.
context: Carpenters and stair builders (O*NET 47-2031) set the balusters of stair, landing and balcony guards. Residential codes allow no opening in a guard that a 4 in (102 mm) sphere can pass (IRC R312.1.3), and inspectors check with a 4 in ball, including the openings next to the newel posts. So the carpenter works out how many balusters a run needs from the clear distance between the posts and the balusters' width, then lays them out with equal openings: one too few and a gap passes the ball however it is spaced, and uneven spacing is redone. Here the guard is at 1:2: 20 mm balusters, 356 mm between the newels and a 51 mm ball, so four balusters can never pass (55.2 mm openings at best), while five (42.7 mm) or six (33.7 mm) can. The count is not given. The six balusters stand on the table behind the guard, three on each arm's side.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Three kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Shoe rail: an oak strip fixed to the table top, 356 mm long along y, 40 mm wide along x and 10 mm tall, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0 (x 28.0 to 32.0 cm, y -17.8 to +17.8 cm); its top is 10 mm above the table. (2) Two newel posts: oak blocks fixed to the table top, 40 x 40 mm and 100 mm tall, centred at x 30.0 cm, y +19.8 cm and y -19.8 cm, sides parallel to x and y. Their inner faces are at y +17.8 and -17.8 cm, flush with the rail's ends, 356 mm apart. (3) Six balusters: loose white-painted maple dowels (plain round cylinders, both ends alike) 20 mm across and 80 mm tall, 18 g each, standing upright on the table on an end: three on the left at x 14.0, 20.0 and 26.0 cm, y +27.0 cm, and three on the right at x 14.0, 20.0 and 26.0 cm, y -27.0 cm (60 mm apart centre to centre). Nothing else is on the table. The 51 mm (2 in) test ball, for example a wooden craft ball, is not in the scene: it is used by the person scoring a real trial. With n balusters spread evenly every opening is (356 - 20 n) / (n + 1) mm: 55.2 mm for four, 42.7 mm for five, 33.7 mm for six, so at least five are needed. The plan layout is a residential guard at 1:2 (a 4 in ball, 1-1/2 in balusters, 712 mm between newels); the heights are not to scale (see fidelity).
scoring: End state: the score is read from where the six balusters are at the last step. A baluster 'stands on the rail' when its axis is within 5 degrees of vertical (either end down), its lowest point is within 2 mm of the rail's top (above or below) and its centre is over the rail's top (within 20 mm of the rail's centre line, x 30.0 cm) between the posts. It is 'down on the guard' when it does not stand on the rail, is tilted more than 5 degrees, its outline seen from above overlaps or comes within 2 mm of the rail's top or a post's top, and its lowest point is at most 20 mm above the rail's top: lying on the rail, or leaning against the rail, a post or another baluster. The 'openings', in order along the rail from the left post: from the left post's inner face to the nearest standing baluster (the distance from its centre to the face less 10 mm), between each pair of neighbouring standing balusters (the distance between their centres less 20 mm: the clear gap at its narrowest), and from the last one to the right post's inner face. With no baluster standing there is one opening of 356 mm. An opening 'passes the ball' when it is 51 mm or more. The 'spread' is the widest opening minus the narrowest. Score 0 if any baluster is down on the guard (a fallen baluster has to be taken away). Otherwise: 1.0 if no opening passes the ball and the spread is 10 mm or less; 0.5 if no opening passes the ball but the spread is over 10 mm; 0.25 if exactly one opening passes the ball and at least four balusters stand on the rail (a guard one baluster short); 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Every outcome: the start (one 356 mm opening) 0; one to three balusters on the rail 0; four spread evenly 0 (five openings of 55.2 mm all pass); four with one wide gap (for example 48, 48, 48, 48 and 84 mm) 0.25; four to six with two or more openings passing 0; five or six with exactly one passing 0.25; five or six with none passing but uneven (for example 35, 50, 35, 50, 36 and 50 mm) 0.5; five evenly (42.7 mm each) or six evenly (33.7 mm) 1.0. Apart from the zero rule for a baluster down on the guard, balusters left on the table, standing on a post's top, held in the air or knocked off the table are ignored. Any baluster may go in any place, and the count is not given. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held with every baluster still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s; one that fell off the table is not waited for) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, offer the 51 mm ball to every opening (it must not pass through) and read each opening at its narrowest with a rule or calipers; a baluster stands when it rests on the rail plumb within 5 degrees (its top within 7 mm of plumb over its 80 mm height).
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The rail and posts are fixed boxes; each baluster is a plain uniform cylinder of the stated size and mass. Only the plan layout is at 1:2: the balusters are cut short to 80 mm (real ones are 34-38 in) and stand free on the rail, a dry layout before they are fixed and the handrail goes on. The scorer sees only the balusters, so one held still with its bottom within 2 mm of the rail counts as standing.
reset_notes: Stand the six balusters back upright on the table: three on the left at x 14.0, 20.0 and 26.0 cm, y +27.0 cm, and three on the right at x 14.0, 20.0 and 26.0 cm, y -27.0 cm. The rail and posts are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
